activities.anchor: their favourite pet and tallies the answers
activities.caption: rebuild the smallest analysis in the world
activities.name: dsFlowOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the tally-chart exercise in its logical order:
items: A question comes first — which pet book to buy?
Data is collected to answer it — the class is polled
The tallies are organised into a form a human can read
The chart is interpreted against the question — dogs beat cats by four
config.why: The whole discipline in miniature: question, collect, organise, interpret — the same loop later run on millions of records.

activities.caption: pair each leg with what its absence costs
activities.name: dsLegsMatch

config.prompt: Data science stands on three legs — pair each with what happens without it:

pairs.right: the work cannot scale past a spreadsheet

config.why: Take any one leg away and the work stops being science — each leg covers a different failure mode.

activities.anchor: Every dataset is built from two kinds of entries
activities.caption: file each summary under the kind of data it serves
activities.name: dsKindSort

config.prompt: File each summary or chart under the kind of data it serves:
config.why: The kind decides the honest summary: an 'average pet' is nonsense while the most common pet is right — and bar charts for categories, scatters and histograms for quantities.

activities.anchor: narrow enough that a map of fatalities
activities.caption: sharpen the question — the Snow decision
activities.name: dsSnowBranch

config.root: London, 1854. Your working question: 'What causes cholera?' — too broad for any dataset to answer.

start.text: The question must become something evidence could decide.

choices.label: Narrow it until a map of deaths could answer it
choices.feedback: Snow's actual move: 'do deaths cluster around a particular water source?' — narrow enough that the Broad Street pump map could settle it.

choices.label: Collect every possible dataset first, decide later
choices.feedback: Data collected before the question is decided collects everything and answers nothing.

choices.label: Ask the data to speak for itself
choices.feedback: It answers whatever you ask — and it answers vague questions vaguely.

hoard.text: The collection drags on; every hypothesis stays alive because none was sharpened.

choices.label: Name the decision, then narrow the question
choices.feedback: A well-formed question names its decision, its deadline and its acceptable error.

vague.text: Vague questions make data decorative — the dashboard fills, the decision does not.

snow.text: A sharp question, a decisive map, a pump handle removed — the outbreak ends.

config.why: Sharp questions make data decisive; vague questions make data decorative — the question comes first.

activities.anchor: its signature is that the data never mentions
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the bias that hides by omission
activities.name: dsBiasCloze

config.text: If customer records only include people who finished signup, every conclusion silently describes %%0%%, not potential customers; if a survey only reaches landlines, it describes %%1%%. Selection bias's signature: the data never %%2%% what it is missing.
config.hint: The signup file describes the completers; the landline survey is stuck in a pre-mobile year; and the missing are never announced.

activities.anchor: prefer fixing the pipeline over hand-editing
activities.caption: find the cleaning rule that got broken
activities.name: dsCleanSpot

config.prompt: One entry in this cleaning log breaks the rules — click it:
lines: Duplicates from the billing-system migration removed.
Viewing hours during the two-week outage recoded as missing, not zero.
Eleven accounts with negative tenure dropped; pipeline bug reported.
A few awkward rows quietly deleted so the retention chart reads cleaner.
config.correction: Never clean silently — document every transformation, and never clean toward the answer you expect.
config.why: Each undocumented edit is a small lie that propagates into every downstream number; a model trained on wrongly joined data is confidently wrong forever.

activities.anchor: do not fit a model and check it against the data
activities.caption: two habits at step four — drag the divider
activities.name: dsEdaCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to meet a new dataset — drag the divider:

before.label: model first
before.text: fit a model, then check it against the data — the classroom habit

after.label: plot first
after.text: look until the data tells you which model would be honest — Tukey's inversion

config.why: Anscombe's quartet: four datasets with identical averages, spreads and fitted lines — and wildly different pictures. Plotting is inspection, not presentation.

activities.anchor: scoring beautifully there and embarrassingly on new data
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the diagnosis
activities.name: dsOverfitPredict

config.q: Your model scores 99% on the data it trained on and 60% on data it has never seen. What is the diagnosis?
choices: Overfitting — it memorised the noise in its training data
Underfitting — the model is too simple
The test set must be wrong
Add more parameters to close the gap
config.why: A flexible model can memorise the noise in its training data; the defence is a held-out test set, and complexity must earn its keep there — a parameter that improves training fit but not test fit is a lie the model tells itself.

activities.caption: file each deliverable under honest reporting or theatre
activities.name: dsCommSort

config.prompt: File each deliverable under honest reporting or theatre:

items.label: a number with its uncertainty range
a truncated axis that doubles the drama
a forecast delivered without a range

config.why: Uncertainty is content, not weakness: a forecast without a range invites decisions the evidence cannot support.
